l.i: num includentem, quo Antigonus occisus est, eundem
annum Julianum duodecimum facere? in quo triennio
fallitur: nam Agrippâ & Caninio coss. Herodes cum So-

main_text.l: §. 2. Qui chronologiæ reformandæ incubuerunt post-
modum, admodum gavisi sunt, de invento charactere
astronomico, quem ipse Josephus illis suppeditare vi-
sus est: quippe qui Ant. Jud. libr. 17: 8. eclipseos ali-
cujus lunaris, sub ipso Herodis decubitu observatæ,
mentionem injicit; quam haud diu ante paschatis cujus-
dam festivitatem inveniendam esse supponunt, aut ex
Josepho se observasse sibi persuadent viri optimi. Nemo
dubitat astronomicas in disciplinâ chronologicâ rationes
solidissima præbere certitudinis documenta, quoniam
cœlestium corporum revolutiones, nec non eclipses lu-
minarium majorum certissimo nituntur calculo. Ve-
rum, cum fieri possit, ut hypothesis, quam viri docti
assumunt, fallat, atque sic qui computum ineunt, se-
met decipiant, prudentia adhibenda est, ne assumptio
alicubi incertior sit. Dixit Josephus Ant. libr. 17 8.
Quod Herodes post multatum pontificatu Matthiam,

page.notes: No marginal notes are printed on this page. Several small asterisks in the text margin at the right and left (beside "lu-", "Herodes" and "Iosephi") are printing marks or stains and are not transcribed. The Greek word marked [?] (ἀνισόρροπον) is hard to read on the scan, and the accents of the Greek in the last paragraph are not fully certain. Printed "Iud." is copied as "Jud.", following the i/j rule. The printed "Ant. Iud. libr. 17: 8." and "Ant. libr. 17 8." are copied as printed. Printed "xlix" and "li" are Roman numerals in the text and are kept as printed. The page ends mid-sentence and the last line is followed by the catchword "ipsâ", so the sentence continues on the next page.
